comparison: Perfect agreement on expression analysis claims (C5, C29-C33, C86-C87, C115-C124). Both evaluations find the immunostaining data and spatial segregation of Gr28a and Gr28b expression well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes systematic validation of GAL4 lines, while peer reviewers highlight clarity of presentation and thorough analysis.

Strong agreement on opposing valence findings (C6, C7, C9, C11, C43-C45, C47-C49). Both evaluations support the VR1 heterologous expression experiments showing attraction vs. avoidance. OpenEval provides detailed validation of controls (C40-C42), while peer reviewers emphasize the striking nature of the chemogenetic results. OpenEval covers additional control claims not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Complete agreement on neuronal inactivation experiments (C12, C51-C53). Both evaluations find the Kir2.1 silencing data convincing with appropriate controls. OpenEval notes functional specialization within Gr28b populations, while peer reviewers affirm necessity of these neurons for bitter avoidance without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on genetic rescue experiments identifying Gr28b.a and Gr28b.c as essential subunits (C14, C54, C59-C60, C68-C69, C93-C96). Both evaluations support the specificity of rescue. OpenEval explicitly addresses caffeine findings (C58) and notes need for further investigation of compensatory mechanisms, while peer reviewers focus on the minimal receptor composition discovery.

Agreement on calcium imaging data supporting differential bitter compound responses (C66-C67, C101-C102). OpenEval addresses these claims along with C64-C65 and C100, finding evidence supported but noting speculation about multiple receptor types. Peer reviewers accept the complexity and partial redundancy as findings rather than limitations.

Partial overlap on calcium imaging claims (C64-C65). OpenEval groups these with broader calcium imaging analysis (R5), while peer reviewers separately evaluate the selectivity of Gr28b.c neurons for bitter compounds. Both find the imaging data well-controlled and convincing.

Agreement on Gr66a mutant analysis (C62-C63). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes the unexpected increase in denatonium/quinine avoidance as important negative evidence suggesting compensatory mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept the data quality without specific concerns.

Minor overlap on caffeine findings (C72 in OpenEval R6 appears in peer R4 context). OpenEval discusses Gr66a mutant effects on multiple compounds including caffeine, while peer reviewers focus on the broader minimal receptor composition. Both support the findings.

Partial overlap where OpenEval R4 addresses caffeine response changes (C56-C58) that peer R6 also evaluates. OpenEval notes increased caffeine avoidance in ΔGr28 mutants requires further investigation, while peer reviewers affirm behavioral assay quality without specific concerns about these claims.

Perfect agreement on evolutionary significance and novelty claims (C16, C74-C76). Both evaluations support the conclusion that Gr28 represents the first receptor subfamily with opposing valence. OpenEval emphasizes literature support for the 'first' claim, while peer reviewers highlight this as a significant contribution to understanding taste receptor complexity.

Divergence in evaluation of multiple receptor type hypothesis (C99-C100). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is speculative and alternative explanations not fully excluded. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the complexity and partial redundancy as demonstrated findings rather than questioning the interpretation.

Minor overlap on sequence analysis (C61, C98). OpenEval R8 focuses on correlative sequence comparisons identifying distinguishing residues, appropriately noting need for experimental validation. Peer R4 addresses broader rescue experiments. Both support the findings with appropriate caveats.

OpenEval evaluates synthesis claims about minimal neuronal ensemble (C88-C89, C91) as SUPPORTED based on expression and functional data. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally affirm the overall conclusions about neuronal organization.

OpenEval evaluates genomic organization claims (C25-C28) as SUPPORTED based on Figure 1B and prior characterization. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers do not raise concerns about the genomic context.

OpenEval evaluates background claims on taste receptor organization (C77-C85) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations to prior work. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this provides important context for interpreting Gr28 functional data.
